name: Pit house
desc: A dwelling dug partly into the ground and roofed with timber, bone or turf, using the earth for insulation.

name: Megalith
desc: Monuments of huge raised stones, from Gobekli Tepe onward, showing early mastery of moving heavy loads.

name: Gobekli Tepe
desc: Monumental enclosures of carved T-shaped stone pillars, the oldest known megalithic site.

name: Thatching
desc: Roofing with layered straw, reed or grass that sheds rain and insulates.

name: Wattle and daub
desc: Woven wooden lattice walls daubed with clay, dung and straw; a building method used for millennia.

name: Longhouse
desc: Long timber-post dwellings of early farming villages that housed extended families and livestock.

name: Stilt house
desc: Houses raised on piles over water or soft ground, protecting against floods and pests.

name: Mortise and tenon
desc: A wood joint where a projecting tenon fits a cut socket, the basis of all timber joinery.

name: Rammed earth
desc: Damp earth compacted in layers inside formwork to make thick, durable walls.

name: Cistern
desc: A sealed underground tank for storing rainwater, made watertight with lime plaster.

name: Dolmen
desc: A chamber tomb of upright stones capped by a large flat stone, an early spanning structure.

name: Dry stone walling
desc: Building walls from fitted stones without mortar, used for houses, terraces and enclosures.

name: Fired brick
desc: Kiln-baked clay bricks that resist water far better than sun-dried mudbrick.

name: Corbel arch
desc: A span made by stepping courses of stone inward until they meet, used in tombs and early vaults.

name: Mastaba
desc: A flat-roofed rectangular Egyptian tomb of mudbrick or stone, the forerunner of the pyramid.

name: Post and lintel
desc: A horizontal beam carried on two upright posts, the simplest structural span.

name: Levee
desc: An earthen embankment along a river that holds back floodwater from fields and towns.

name: Embankment dam
desc: A dam of compacted earth or rock fill; the oldest dam type, as at Jawa in Jordan.

name: Ashlar masonry
desc: Finely dressed rectangular stone blocks laid in regular courses with thin joints.

name: Gravity dam
desc: A massive masonry or concrete dam that resists water pressure by its own weight.

name: Pyramid construction
desc: Quarrying, hauling and stacking millions of stone blocks with ramps and levers to build Egypt's pyramids.

name: Column
desc: A vertical structural member carrying beams or arches, first carved in stone in Egypt.

name: Plumb bob
desc: A weight hung on a string to establish a true vertical when building walls.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza
desc: Khufu's pyramid, the tallest human-made structure for nearly four millennia.

name: Rock-cut architecture
desc: Carving tombs, temples and dwellings directly out of solid rock.

name: Arch
desc: A curved span of wedge-shaped units held in compression, carrying loads far wider than a lintel.

name: Stonehenge
desc: A Neolithic ring of sarsen uprights capped with lintels joined by woodworking-style joints.

name: Ziggurat
desc: A Mesopotamian stepped temple tower of mudbrick faced with baked brick.

name: Barrel vault
desc: An arch extended along its length to roof a long space.

name: Log building
desc: Walls of horizontal logs notched together at the corners, typical of forested northern regions.

name: Building code
desc: Rules setting standards for building safety, first recorded in the Code of Hammurabi.

name: Beehive tomb
desc: A Mycenaean tholos tomb roofed with a corbelled stone dome.

name: Cyclopean masonry
desc: Massive unworked limestone boulders fitted together without mortar, as at Mycenae.

name: Windcatcher
desc: A tower that catches wind and drives it through a building for passive cooling and ventilation.

name: Treasury of Atreus
desc: A Mycenaean tholos whose corbelled dome was the widest in the world for over a millennium.

name: Roof tiles
desc: Fired clay tiles laid in overlapping rows to make a durable, fireproof roof.

name: Siloam tunnel
desc: A water tunnel cut through rock under Jerusalem by two teams digging from opposite ends.

name: Aqueduct
desc: A built channel carrying water by gravity over long distances to a city.

name: Classical order
desc: The Doric, Ionic and Corinthian systems of proportioned columns and entablatures.

name: Tunnel of Eupalinos
desc: A 1 km aqueduct tunnel on Samos dug from both ends with geometric surveying.

name: Crane
desc: A lifting machine using pulleys and a jib, first used by Greek builders to raise stone blocks.

name: Timber framing
desc: A structural skeleton of heavy squared timbers joined with pegged joints, infilled between.

name: Pontoon bridge
desc: A floating bridge of boats lashed together and decked over.

name: Parthenon
desc: The Doric marble temple of Athens, a model of refined proportion and optical correction.

name: Dougong
desc: Interlocking wooden bracket sets that carry the wide eaves of Chinese timber buildings.

name: Roman aqueduct
desc: Graded channels on arcades and tunnels that supplied Roman cities with abundant water.

name: Lighthouse
desc: A tower with a light to guide ships, beginning with the Pharos of Alexandria.

name: Arch bridge
desc: A bridge carried on masonry arches, perfected by Roman engineers.

name: Inverted siphon
desc: A sealed pipe that carries water down and across a valley and back up by pressure.

name: Formwork
desc: Temporary moulds that hold wet concrete in shape until it sets.

name: Insula
desc: Multi-storey Roman apartment blocks of brick-faced concrete housing most urban residents.

name: Dome
desc: A hemispherical vault, an arch rotated about its axis, enclosing large spaces without columns.

name: Groin vault
desc: Two barrel vaults crossing at right angles, concentrating loads onto corner piers.

name: Hypocaust
desc: Roman underfloor heating that drew hot furnace gases through spaces under floors and walls.

name: Arch dam
desc: A dam curved upstream that transfers water pressure into the valley walls.

name: Pile driver
desc: A machine that drops a heavy weight to drive piles into the ground for foundations.

name: Cofferdam
desc: A temporary watertight enclosure pumped dry so that foundations can be built underwater.

name: De architectura
desc: Vitruvius's treatise on building, materials and machines, the only surviving ancient architecture manual.

name: Pont du Gard
desc: A three-tiered Roman aqueduct bridge in southern France, built of dry-laid ashlar.

name: Colosseum
desc: Rome's amphitheater for some 50,000 spectators, built on vaulted concrete and stone arcades.

name: Buttress dam
desc: A dam with a thin wall braced by buttresses on the downstream side, saving material.

name: Pantheon, Rome
desc: Hadrian's temple whose unreinforced concrete dome stayed the world's largest for over a millennium.

name: Squinch
desc: A small arch across the corner of a square room that lets a round dome sit on it, developed in Sasanian Persia.

name: Pagoda
desc: A tiered tower, often of timber, whose flexible central post helped it survive earthquakes.

name: Pendentive
desc: A curved triangle of vaulting that carries a dome over a square base, as in Hagia Sophia.

name: Hagia Sophia
desc: Justinian's church whose great dome on pendentives became a model for Byzantine and Ottoman buildings.

name: Pointed arch
desc: An arch with a pointed crown that pushes less sideways, used in Islamic and later Gothic building.

name: Stepwell
desc: An Indian well or reservoir reached by descending flights of steps, storing water through dry seasons.

name: Anji Bridge
desc: The oldest standing open-spandrel segmental stone arch bridge, built by Li Chun in China.

name: Muqarnas
desc: Honeycomb-like corbelled vaulting used to transition between surfaces in Islamic architecture.

name: Rib vault
desc: A vault built on a framework of crossing stone ribs, lighter than solid vaults.

name: Yingzao Fashi
desc: A Song dynasty building manual that standardized modular timber construction.

name: Gothic architecture
desc: A style combining rib vaults and pointed arches to build tall, light-filled churches.

name: Flying buttress
desc: An external arched prop that carries vault thrust away from walls, allowing large windows.

name: Chimney
desc: A flue that draws smoke out of a building and improves the draft of a fire.

name: Tracery
desc: Stone ribs dividing Gothic windows to support large areas of glass.

name: Fan vault
desc: An English Gothic vault of cone-shaped clusters of equal ribs.

name: Hammerbeam roof
desc: A timber roof with short cantilevered beams, letting it span wide halls such as Westminster Hall.

name: Florence Cathedral
desc: Brunelleschi's double-shell brick dome, built without centering, the largest masonry dome.

name: Truss
desc: A rigid framework of triangles that carries loads efficiently through members in tension and compression.

name: Strength of materials
desc: The science of how materials and beams resist loads, founded in Galileo's Two New Sciences.

name: Cast iron pipe
desc: Pressure pipes of cast iron, first laid at Versailles, that made large water mains possible.

name: Plate glass
desc: Large flat sheets of cast and polished glass for windows and mirrors.

name: Euler-Bernoulli beam theory
desc: A mathematical model of beam bending that underlies the design of girders and frames.

name: Lightning rod
desc: Benjamin Franklin's grounded metal rod that protects buildings from lightning strikes.

name: Hydraulic lime
desc: Lime that sets underwater, rediscovered by John Smeaton for the Eddystone Lighthouse.

name: Eddystone Lighthouse
desc: Smeaton's dovetailed granite tower on a wave-swept reef, a founding work of civil engineering.

name: The Iron Bridge
desc: The first major bridge made of cast iron, spanning the Severn at Coalbrookdale.

name: Cast-iron architecture
desc: Buildings framed and faced with cast-iron columns and beams, cheap, fast and fire-resistant.

name: Ditherington Flax Mill
desc: The first iron-framed building, often called the grandfather of skyscrapers.

name: Water supply network
desc: Pumped, pressurized citywide water mains delivering water to buildings, as at Philadelphia.

name: Suspension bridge
desc: A deck hung from iron chains or cables slung between towers, spanning great distances.

name: Slow sand filter
desc: Beds of sand that filter and biologically clean drinking water for a whole town.

name: Tunnelling shield
desc: Brunel's movable iron frame that protects workers digging through soft ground, used for the Thames Tunnel.

name: Menai Suspension Bridge
desc: Telford's wrought-iron chain bridge, the first large suspension bridge.

name: Central heating
desc: A single boiler or furnace heating a whole building through pipes or ducts.

name: Balloon framing
desc: Light frames of sawn lumber and machine-made nails, letting houses be built quickly by few workers.

name: Prefabrication
desc: Making building components in a factory for rapid assembly on site.

name: Steam shovel
desc: A steam-powered digging machine that moved earth for railways and canals.

name: Truss bridge
desc: Bridges of triangulated timber or iron frames, built by the thousand for railways.

name: Caisson
desc: A pressurized watertight chamber sunk to bedrock so foundations can be dug below water.

name: Thames Tunnel
desc: The first tunnel built under a navigable river, dug with Brunel's shield.

name: Plate girder bridge
desc: A bridge carried by deep riveted iron or steel girders, common for short railway spans.

name: Ferrocement
desc: Thin cement mortar over iron mesh, first used by Lambot for a boat.

name: I-beam
desc: A rolled beam with an I-shaped cross-section that puts material where bending stress is highest.

name: Pneumatic drill
desc: A percussive rock drill driven by steam and later compressed air, speeding tunneling and demolition.

name: Box girder bridge
desc: A bridge built from hollow box-section girders, first as the wrought-iron tubes of the Britannia Bridge.

name: Britannia Bridge
desc: Stephenson's wrought-iron tubular railway bridge over the Menai Strait.

name: Water tower
desc: An elevated tank that keeps water mains pressurized and stores reserve supply.

name: The Crystal Palace
desc: Paxton's prefabricated iron and glass exhibition hall, assembled in months.

name: Safety elevator
desc: Otis's elevator with a brake that catches the car if the rope breaks, making tall buildings usable.

name: Reinforced concrete
desc: Concrete with embedded iron or steel bars to carry tension, the dominant modern structural material.

name: Radiator
desc: A cast-iron heat exchanger that releases heat from steam or hot water into a room.

name: Fire escape
desc: External iron stairs and balconies that give occupants a way out of burning buildings.

name: Ground freezing
desc: Freezing waterlogged soil with brine pipes so shafts and tunnels can be dug safely.

name: Oriel Chambers
desc: A Liverpool office building with one of the first metal-framed glass curtain walls.

name: Cantilever bridge
desc: A bridge built from arms projecting from piers, which can be erected without falsework.

name: Fire sprinkler system
desc: Ceiling pipes with heat-triggered heads that release water directly onto a fire.

name: Eads Bridge
desc: The first major bridge built of steel, with tubular arches over the Mississippi.

name: Tunnel boring machine
desc: A machine with a rotating cutting head that excavates a full tunnel face continuously.

name: Brooklyn Bridge
desc: The first steel-wire suspension bridge, whose caisson foundations reached bedrock under the East River.

name: Steel frame
desc: A skeleton of steel columns and beams that carries all loads, freeing walls from bearing weight.

name: Skyscraper
desc: A tall, continuously habitable building made possible by steel frames and elevators.

name: Rapid sand filter
desc: A compact filter using coagulants and backwashing to treat large volumes of water quickly.

name: Home Insurance Building
desc: A Chicago office tower often called the first skyscraper for its load-bearing metal frame.

name: Glass brick
desc: Hollow glass blocks that admit light through walls and roofs; first patented as blown glass bricks by Falconnier in 1886.

name: Eiffel Tower
desc: A 300 m wrought-iron lattice tower of prefabricated riveted parts, the tallest structure of its time.

name: Forth Bridge
desc: A giant steel cantilever railway bridge in Scotland built after the Tay Bridge disaster.

name: Earthquake engineering
desc: The study and design of structures to survive seismic shaking, born in Meiji Japan.

name: Wainwright Building
desc: Louis Sullivan's St. Louis tower that defined the expressive tall office building.

name: Glued laminated timber
desc: Layers of lumber glued into large beams and arches stronger than any single log.

name: Moving walkway
desc: A slow conveyor belt that carries pedestrians along a level or gentle incline.

name: Escalator
desc: A motorized moving staircase that carries large crowds between floors.

name: Hyperboloid structure
desc: Shukhov's lattice towers of straight steel bars forming a doubly curved, light and stiff shell.

name: Tensile structure
desc: Structures whose roofs are carried by members in tension only, such as steel cable nets and membranes.

name: Gridshell
desc: A doubly curved shell made from a lattice grid, first built by Shukhov.

name: Concrete mixer
desc: A rotating drum that combines cement, aggregate and water into uniform concrete.

name: Concrete block
desc: Standard hollow blocks of cast concrete, a cheap and fast walling material.

name: Asphalt shingle
desc: Mat roofing shingles coated with asphalt and granules, the most common North American roof.

name: Air conditioning
desc: Willis Carrier's system for controlling indoor temperature and humidity with refrigeration.

name: Flatiron Building
desc: A triangular steel-framed New York skyscraper on a narrow wedge-shaped lot.

name: Precast concrete
desc: Concrete elements cast in a factory and lifted into place, speeding construction.

name: Shotcrete
desc: Concrete sprayed through a hose at high speed onto a surface, used for tunnel linings and slopes.

name: Space frame
desc: A three-dimensional truss of interlocking struts that spans large roofs with little material.

name: Tilt-up construction
desc: Casting concrete wall panels flat on site and tilting them upright with a crane.

name: Water chlorination
desc: Adding chlorine to public water supplies to kill pathogens, sharply cutting typhoid and cholera.

name: Kit house
desc: Mail-order houses shipped as precut lumber and parts for owner assembly.

name: Immersed tube tunnel
desc: Prefabricated tunnel sections floated into place and sunk into a trench on the seabed or riverbed.

name: Slip forming
desc: Pouring concrete continuously into a form that climbs steadily, used for silos, towers and cores.

name: Ready-mix concrete
desc: Concrete batched at a plant and delivered in mixer trucks to the site.

name: Drywall
desc: Gypsum board faced with paper that replaced wet plaster for interior walls.

name: Curtain wall
desc: A non-structural outer skin, usually glass, hung on a building's frame.

name: Bulldozer
desc: A tracked tractor with a front blade for pushing earth and clearing sites.

name: Soil mechanics
desc: Terzaghi's science of soil behavior under load, the basis of foundation engineering.

name: Thin-shell structure
desc: Curved reinforced concrete shells only centimeters thick that span wide roofs.

name: Geodesic dome
desc: A dome of triangulated struts on a sphere, first built for the Jena planetarium and popularized by Fuller.

name: Concrete pump
desc: A machine that pumps liquid concrete through pipes to where it is poured.

name: Prestressed concrete
desc: Freyssinet's concrete precompressed by tensioned steel tendons, allowing long slender spans.

name: HVAC
desc: Integrated building systems for heating, ventilation and cooling, standard in large buildings.

name: Empire State Building
desc: A 102-storey steel-framed tower built in about a year, the world's tallest for four decades.

name: Building insulation
desc: Glass wool and other materials in walls and roofs that cut heat loss and gain.

name: Insulated glazing
desc: Double or triple panes sealed around a gas gap to reduce heat transfer through windows.

name: Hoover Dam
desc: A concrete arch-gravity dam on the Colorado River, cooled with embedded pipes as it set.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
desc: A 1,280 m steel suspension span, the longest in the world when it opened.

name: Bailey bridge
desc: A portable prefabricated steel truss bridge assembled by hand without heavy equipment.

name: Air-supported structure
desc: A fabric membrane held up by slight internal air pressure from fans, covering large spaces.

name: Tensegrity
desc: Structures of isolated compression struts held in a continuous net of tension cables.

name: Slurry wall
desc: A concrete wall cast in a trench held open by bentonite slurry, used for deep basements.

name: Large-panel-system building
desc: Mass housing assembled from storey-height precast concrete panels, widespread in the Soviet bloc.

name: Hydraulic excavator
desc: A digging machine with a hydraulic boom and bucket on a rotating cab.

name: Cable-stayed bridge
desc: A bridge deck held directly by straight cables running down from towers.

name: Finite element method
desc: Computer analysis that divides a structure into small elements to compute stresses, first used for aircraft and buildings.

name: Storm surge barrier
desc: Movable gates across an estuary that close against storm tides.

name: Geotextile
desc: Permeable synthetic fabrics laid in soil to separate, filter, drain and reinforce it.

name: Modular building
desc: Buildings assembled from whole factory-made volumetric modules.

name: Retractable roof
desc: A stadium or arena roof that opens and closes on motorized tracks.

name: New Austrian tunnelling method
desc: Tunneling that uses the surrounding rock as support, lined quickly with shotcrete and bolts.

name: Mechanically stabilized earth
desc: Henri Vidal's soil reinforced with layered strips, forming retaining walls and embankments.

name: Tube structure
desc: Fazlur Khan's system where the outer frame acts as a hollow tube, enabling very tall towers economically.

name: Fiber-reinforced concrete
desc: Concrete with dispersed steel, glass or synthetic fibers that improve crack resistance.

name: Reverse osmosis
desc: Pushing water through a semi-permeable membrane to remove salts, used for desalination and purification.

name: Habitat 67
desc: Moshe Safdie's Montreal housing complex of stacked precast concrete modules.

name: Seismic base isolation
desc: Flexible bearings under a building that decouple it from ground shaking during earthquakes.

name: Olympiastadion Munich
desc: Frei Otto's stadium roofed with a sweeping cable-net and acrylic tensile canopy.

name: Sydney Opera House
desc: Utzon's shells built from precast concrete ribs, an early computer-analysed structure.

name: CN Tower
desc: A 553 m slipformed concrete tower in Toronto, the world's tallest free-standing structure for decades.

name: Tuned mass damper
desc: A large tuned weight that counteracts the sway of tall buildings in wind and earthquakes.

name: Building automation
desc: Computerized control of a building's heating, cooling, lighting and security.

name: Extradosed bridge
desc: A hybrid of girder and cable-stayed bridge with low towers and shallow stay cables.

name: Roller-compacted concrete
desc: Dry concrete spread and compacted with earthmoving rollers, making dams fast and cheap.

name: Self-consolidating concrete
desc: Highly fluid concrete that flows around dense reinforcement without vibration.

name: Building information modeling
desc: Shared 3D digital models holding a building's geometry and data through design, construction and operation.

name: Passive house
desc: A standard for airtight, superinsulated buildings with heat-recovery ventilation that need little heating.

name: Green building
desc: Design and rating systems such as BREEAM and LEED that reduce a building's environmental impact.

name: Building-integrated photovoltaics
desc: Solar cells built into roofs, facades and glazing as part of the building envelope.

name: Channel Tunnel
desc: A 50 km rail tunnel under the English Channel bored by eleven TBMs.

name: Cross-laminated timber
desc: Large panels of lumber layers glued at right angles, the core material of mass timber buildings.

name: Delta Works
desc: The Dutch system of dams, sluices and surge barriers protecting the southwestern delta from the sea.

name: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
desc: A Japanese suspension bridge with a 1,991 m central span, longest in the world for over two decades.

name: Millau Viaduct
desc: A multi-span cable-stayed bridge in France with the tallest bridge piers in the world.

name: Self-healing concrete
desc: Concrete containing bacteria or capsules that seal cracks automatically.

name: Burj Khalifa
desc: The world's tallest building at 828 m, built on a buttressed concrete core.

name: Construction 3D printing
desc: Robotic extrusion of concrete layer by layer to build walls and whole houses.

name: Gotthard Base Tunnel
desc: A 57 km railway tunnel under the Alps, the world's longest.

name: Plyscraper
desc: A high-rise built mainly of mass timber, such as Norway's 85 m Mjostarnet.
